external_entities.name: developer
external_entities.description: A developer who pushes branches and may manually start a rebuild of main.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
external_entities.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand.

external_entities.name: public package registry
external_entities.description: The public package registry reached during dependency resolution.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet

processes.name: till software
processes.description: Till software running as a container on store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: running the till software as a container

processes.name: store server
processes.description: A small server in each store's back office that runs the till software and polls for releases.
processes.source_excerpt: Each store has a small server in the back office
processes.notes: Represents the store servers across about 1,200 stores.

processes.name: build runner
processes.description: The build component that fetches source, resolves dependencies, produces container images, and starts deployment.
processes.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source, resolves the dependency lockfile and produces a container image.
processes.notes: Any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of main by hand; that path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

processes.name: deploy controller
processes.description: The controller that records the current estate image release and serves release information to store servers.
processes.source_excerpt: The deploy controller runs on the corporate network and holds one record: which image sha the estate should be on.

data_stores.name: git server
data_stores.description: The self-hosted Git server holding developer branches and the source used for builds.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server
data_stores.notes: Nobody has documented whether the git server encrypts what it stores.

data_stores.name: image registry
data_stores.description: The registry holding finished container images tagged with commit SHAs.
data_stores.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_stores.notes: The registry allows the pull. Nobody has documented whether the image registry encrypts what it stores.

data_flows.name: push branches
data_flows.description: A developer pushes a branch to the self-hosted Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Developers push their branches to our self-hosted git server

data_flows.name: fetch source
data_flows.description: The build runner fetches merged source from the Git server.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The build runner picks the merge up, fetches the source

data_flows.name: push image
data_flows.description: The build runner pushes the finished container image to the registry.
data_flows.source_excerpt: It pushes the finished image to our image registry
data_flows.notes: Images are tagged with the commit sha.
data_flows.data_description: finished container image tagged with the commit SHA

data_flows.name: set release
data_flows.description: The build runner asks the deploy controller to make an image the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When the image is pushed the runner calls the deploy controller and asks it to make that image the current release.
data_flows.notes: The runner uses a shared build token that is the same for every pipeline and has not been rotated since the pipeline was set up.
data_flows.data_description: image SHA and shared build token

data_flows.name: ask current release
data_flows.description: A store server asks the deploy controller which image SHA is the current release.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every store server asks the deploy controller once a minute what the current release is
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the controller.
data_flows.data_description: request for the current release image SHA

data_flows.name: pull image
data_flows.description: A store server pulls the current container image from the registry when its release differs.
data_flows.source_excerpt: if it differs from what it is running it pulls that image from the registry
data_flows.notes: Nobody has written down what a store server presents to the registry.

data_flows.name: resolve dependencies
data_flows.description: The build runner reaches the public package registry while resolving the dependency lockfile.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Dependency resolution reaches out to the public package registry on the internet
data_flows.notes: The runner does not verify signatures on what it downloads.
data_flows.data_description: dependency packages resolved from the lockfile

data_flows.name: kick off rebuild
data_flows.description: A developer logs in to the build runner and manually starts a rebuild of main.
data_flows.source_excerpt: any developer can log in to the build runner and kick off a rebuild of `main` by hand
data_flows.notes: That path does not require a merge and is not reviewed.

trust_boundaries.name: corporate network
trust_boundaries.description: The corporate network containing the Git server and deploy controller.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: which sits on the corporate network

trust_boundaries.name: build environment
trust_boundaries.description: The separate environment containing the build runner and image registry.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The runner lives in its own build environment, separate from the corporate network.

trust_boundaries.name: store estate
trust_boundaries.description: The in-store estate containing the store servers.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The image registry is reachable from the store estate over the WAN.

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The public internet where the public package registry is located.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: the public package registry on the internet

assumptions.assumption: The till software handles business-critical operating data because it is the till software deployed throughout the in-store estate.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the till software as the software running the in-store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The store server handles business-critical deployment data because it polls for and retrieves the estate's current release.
assumptions.basis: The store server asks for the current release and pulls the corresponding image.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner handles business-critical build artifacts and source because it fetches source and produces container images.
assumptions.basis: The build runner fetches source, resolves dependencies, and produces a container image.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller handles business-critical deployment records because it holds the image SHA that the estate should run.
assumptions.basis: The deploy controller holds the current release record.

assumptions.assumption: The Git server stores confidential data because it stores source code and developer branches.
assumptions.basis: The Git server holds developer branches and source code, which are commercially sensitive build materials.

assumptions.assumption: The image registry stores confidential data because it stores finished container images for deployment.
assumptions.basis: The registry holds finished container images used to deploy the in-store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The developer-to-Git flow carries business-critical data because it carries source branches for the in-store build pipeline.
assumptions.basis: Developers push branches that feed the build and deployment pipeline.

assumptions.assumption: The Git-to-runner flow carries business-critical data because it carries source code used to produce the deployed image.
assumptions.basis: The build runner fetches source for the estate's container image.

assumptions.assumption: The runner-to-registry flow carries business-critical data because it carries the finished image deployed to the stores.
assumptions.basis: The finished container image is stored for deployment to the store estate.

assumptions.assumption: The runner-to-controller flow carries credentials because it uses the shared build token.
assumptions.basis: The source explicitly states that the runner uses a shared build token.

assumptions.assumption: The runner-to-controller flow carries business-critical data because it sets the image SHA for the estate's current release.
assumptions.basis: The runner asks the controller to make the image the current release.

assumptions.assumption: The store-server-to-controller flow carries business-critical data because it requests the estate's current release image SHA.
assumptions.basis: Store servers ask the deploy controller what the current release is.

assumptions.assumption: The store-server-to-registry flow carries business-critical data because it pulls the deployed container image.
assumptions.basis: Store servers pull the current image from the registry.

assumptions.assumption: The dependency-resolution flow carries business-critical data because dependency packages are inputs to the build artifact deployed to the stores.
assumptions.basis: The runner resolves dependencies and produces the deployed container image.

assumptions.assumption: The build runner is internally exposed because it is described as running in the organization's separate build environment and is accessed by developers.
assumptions.basis: The source places the runner in the separate build environment and says developers log in to it.

assumptions.assumption: The Git server is internally exposed because it sits on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source places the self-hosted Git server on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The deploy controller is internally exposed because it runs on the corporate network.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the deploy controller runs on the corporate network.

assumptions.assumption: The store server is internally exposed because it is located in the back office of an in-store estate.
assumptions.basis: The source places the store server in each store's back office.

assumptions.assumption: The till software is internally exposed because it runs on store servers in the in-store estate.
assumptions.basis: The source describes the till software as running on store servers in the stores.
